label: FOSC 600-D in-line closure, 504 splices
notes: The feeder/trunk joint the catalogue could not describe: 288-fibre ribbon cable is sold here and every other closure held 48 splices or fewer, so a 288-fibre through-joint read as over-stuffed in every box a designer could pick. Figures are CommScope's FOSC 600 datasheet, table 'Tray (and splice) capacity of closures': 600 D In-line = 7 D trays (504 splices), 600 D Butt = 9 trays (648), 600 C In-line = 3 trays (216). 504 is 7 trays x 72, and 72 is the D tray with six SM12 modules from the same sheet's tray ordering table. Two caveats travel with that number. First, capacity is a function of the tray ordered, not of the housing: the 2016 revision of the same CommScope datasheet (PS-322662-EU) prints 672 for this box in-line and 288 for the 600 C, because it counts 96 splices per D tray, which is the SMOUV 45 mm module; order the 96-way modules and 672 is real, order standard 72-way trays and 504 is the ceiling - the row takes 504 so an order of standard trays is not over-subscribed on paper. Second, ribbon splicing has its own count: the 2016 sheet prints 1152 on 4 ribbon trays (288 per tray), so a 288-fibre ribbon joint fits one tray, well inside this row. A joint of 288 splices or fewer no longer needs this trunk dome: fosc-600c-inline-288 is the same 600 C housing with 96-way D trays (3 x 96), 152 mm high rather than 254 mm, so this row now answers a joint past 288 and a 432F trunk. Cable side, from the same sheet: cables up to 35 mm and 1728 fibres, up to 16 separate cable ports, and the 4 ports here are one 4-port gel block - the order code 8 ships two blocks and gives 8 ports. This is a feeder/trunk closure with no drop ports; use a NAP for the last splice. Confirm the SKU and its trays against the purchased closure's own datasheet before ordering - capacity, ports and tray type all move with the order code - replace this row with the closure actually bought, and with the datasheet for the SKU ordered.
